# Motivation for Recovery

Motivation naturally rises and falls during recovery. It is not a permanent feeling. Long-term recovery relies less on waiting to "feel ready" and more on reconnecting with values and consequences regularly. Motivation becomes more stable when you keep your reasons visible and specific.

A practical strategy is to separate short-term urges from long-term goals. Urges ask, *"How do I feel right now?"* Recovery asks, *"What life am I building?"*

## Values-to-Action Exercise

Use this exercise to connect what matters most to one concrete step.

1.  **What I want to protect.** *Examples: health, family, stability, career, self-respect.*

    \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

2.  **How alcohol harms this.** Be specific about the impact.

    \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

3.  **One recovery action this week.** Keep it small, clear, and doable. *Examples: attend one meeting, remove alcohol from home, call a support person, leave early from a risky situation.*

    \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

::: callout
### Make It Stick

-   Write your answer to #1 somewhere visible (phone, notes, wallet)
-   Review it when urges show up
-   Focus on action, not feeling
:::
